named_events.loss_description: only one significant core melt nuclear event paid by the insurance market
Following the Fukushima accident in March 2011, an extensive review of the Syndicate's potential catastrophe exposure was undertaken, and exposure is considered to be limited.

The largest insured windstorm loss to date was from a spares warehouse on a nuclear site from Hurricane Andrew in 1992. While the warehouse was damaged, with losses in the region of $200m, there was no damage to the nuclear unit.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 1176 reported a prior year reserve release of GBP 8.3 million in 2018, primarily attributed to favorable claims development within the nuclear property class. No specific events were explicitly linked to this release. The report mentions several named events, including historical ones like Three Mile Island (1979) and Fukushima (2011), as well as recent hurricanes like Harvey, Irma, Maria (2017), Florence, and Michael (2018), none of which resulted in significant claims advices for the Syndicate. Losses from 2016 events (fire in France, contamination in a fuel plant, Asian nuclear power plant loss) were within forecast expectations.
